subject: Proposal: Multi-year price-insurance + seasonal ramp credits
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Dunham <sara.dunham@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Multi-year price-insurance + seasonal ramp credits

Hi Sara —

Following our renewal sync, attached is a concise proposal that addresses Acme's top two concerns: protecting unit pricing against market increases and smoothing budget impact across the year. The proposal is framed as a "price-insurance" multi-year prepay with a seasonal ramp-credit schedule. Key bullets: 

- Structure: 3-year commitment with an annual prepay (invoice at start of each year).
- Price benefit: blended effective discount that increases with tenure; pick-your-tier (we show 10% / 12% / 15% as anchors).
- Ramp credits: credits unlock quarterly to accommodate Acme's seasonal spike profile; unused credits roll forward for the year with a single annual true-up.
- Make-good / safety buffer: optional 10% safety buffer in year 1 to avoid overrun exposure; true-up at year-end.
- Capacity guarantee: burst access to additional capacity at negotiated uplift rate (if you hit 120% of committed throughput).

I've attached a one-page summary and a term schedule workbook that lays out example cash flows and the expected unit economics at different usage curves. This is intentionally written for procurement/legal consumption.

Can you confirm whether procurement needs an alternative billing cadence (PO per year vs single PO for term)? If useful I can produce a single-page PO-ready summary for your finance team.

Suggested next steps:
- Please review the one-pager with procurement and legal;
- If the structure looks reasonable, we'll prepare a redline-friendly SOW and a short mutual action plan (MAP) with checkpoints at 30/90/180 days.

Appreciate a quick read — happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: ACME_MultiYear_Price_Insurance_OnePager_v2.pdf, ACME_Term_Schedule_Summary.xlsx

From: Sara Dunham <sara.dunham@acme-enterprises.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Multi-year price-insurance + seasonal ramp credits

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for this — the one-pager helps. A few clarifying questions from procurement/legal and finance: 

1) Billing cadence: our default is one PO per fiscal year. We can do annual prepay (OK) but cannot accept multi-year single payment. Will the discount tiers still apply if we prepay each year separately?

2) True-up / make-good: how does the true-up interact with the safety buffer? If we prepay and then underuse, do you provide credits back to our account or only roll forward to next year?

3) Legal: we need a short summary of termination rights and an SLA credit bucket tied to the committed throughput. Also are there standard audit / data governance attachments you require?

4) Pricing cap: we like the idea of price protection but need a guaranteed cap on per-token price (or equivalent unit) for the term. Can you add that to the one-pager?

If you can update the one-pager addressing these points I can circulate with procurement and get back with preferred billing cadence and whether procurement needs a PO template. Also including procurement@acme-enterprises.com so they have the doc.

Cheers,
Sara Dunham
Head of Product Integrations | Acme Enterprises
+1 (617) 555-8800

Subject: Fwd: Proposal: Multi-year price-insurance + seasonal ramp credits — suggested edits

Vanessa / Marcus —

Quick draft back for Acme based on Sara's questions. Main moves I recommend:

- Annual-billed prepay: keep annual invoicing (one PO / year) but keep the multi-year discounted schedule active. In practice that means the year-2 and year-3 discount tiers are contingent on remaining in the program; if Acme renews at the start of year 2 they receive the higher tier for that year. This satisfies Acme's AP constraints while keeping term economics.

- True-up language: propose credits roll forward for the next 12 months as default. If Acme requests refund cash, allow it only at year-end and subject to a 3% processing fee (keeps accounting predictable).

- Safety buffer: convert the 10% safety buffer into an optional add-on SKU that is billed as part of the annual prepay but can be consumed first. If not consumed, it rolls forward as credits (no cash refund except at final year true-up).

- Price cap: add an explicit per-unit price cap for the term (we suggest $0.0012 / token equivalent in the workbook) and a simple formula in the term schedule showing effective blended price.

- SLA/termination: standard SLA credits and 90-day termination for convenience after year 1. For material breach (data or security) escalate to CS and legal.

I've attached a revised one-pager (ACME_MultiYear_Price_Insurance_OnePager_v3.pdf) and a short excerpt you can send to procurement that lists PO language. If this looks good I can spin the redline SOW.

-Marketing / pitch language is intentionally simple — procurement wants bullet + numerical examples.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Sara —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions. Per our internal review (attached is the updated one-pager and a short PO-ready summary):

- Billing cadence: we confirm annual invoicing is fine. The multi-year discount schedule remains valid provided Acme renews at each annual renewal checkpoint; the confirmatory PO each year is the renewal trigger.

- True-up / make-good: default behavior is credits roll forward for 12 months. If Acme requests a cash refund at the year-end true-up, we can accommodate with a 3% processing fee. We added explicit language in section 2 of the one-pager.

- Safety buffer: converted to an optional add-on SKU that is billed up front and consumed first; unused buffer credits roll forward into the following 12 months.

- Price cap: we've added a per-unit cap of $0.0012 / token-equivalent for the agreed tiers; see the term schedule workbook for worked examples.

- SLA / termination: standard SLA credits apply; termination for convenience after 12 months with 90 days' notice (we'll provide the formal clause in the SOW).

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement: please confirm if Acme will accept one PO per fiscal year that references the Master Term Schedule (attached).
2) Legal: once procurement confirms billing cadence we'll route a short SOW + MSA to your counsel for redlines.

Would you like a 20-minute wrap-up call Monday morning PT? I can include Ben and Marcus on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
